body: Direct listing Sept 2020 (~$10). Low ~$6 in late 2022 (all-time low $6.55 by May 2022; ~$5.9 Dec 2022), -87% from the Jan 2021 meme peak (~$45) [peak unverified]. P/S fell from 35x (Sep 2021) to 8.5x (Sep 2022). Then: first GAAP profit Q4 2022 and consecutive profitable quarters (S&P 500 entry Sept 2024); AIP launched 2023 with 'bootcamps' (560 done by Feb 2024) that accelerated US commercial deals; Q1 2026 revenue +85% y/y to $1.633bn. Peak ~$207 (Nov 2025) [unverified] ≈ 35x from the low. P/S hit 137x (Aug 2025, Motley Fool) — the stock outran even 85% growth. Split: overwhelmingly rerating (P/S 8.5x -> 137x ≈ 16x) vs revenue ~2.5x. By Nov 13 2026: ~-36% from ATH, ~60x sales, forward P/E ~85 vs ~200 at peak — multiple compression despite growth. EARLY SIGNAL visible 2023: sustained GAAP profitability (index eligibility), accelerating US commercial customer count and deal size after bootcamps, rule-of-40 score rising, while the stock was at ~8x sales. Who caught it: retail community, Wedbush's Dan Ives, ARK (bought 2022-23) [unverified]. LESSON: real fundamental acceleration started it, but a 16x multiple expansion means future returns depend on keeping hype; Motley Fool notes only 7 other software firms ever traded >100x sales and all fell >=70% from peak valuation.

data.early_signals: GAAP profitability -> S&P eligibility; AIP bootcamps; US commercial acceleration at 8x sales
data.lesson: >100x sales base rate is brutal even with 85% growth

title: Palantir 2022-2026: ~35x on AIP, mostly multiple, then -36%
